prompt: I am going to rework rates.py next week and I want a safety net first. Please write tests under tests/ that pin down what this shipping label tool does today, so that after the refactor I can tell if I changed what it computes or prints. The behaviour as it stands is the contract, including the odd parts customers and the warehouse already rely on. You can read all of the code, but do not change any of it, the existing tests, the CLI, or the package files. Keep the suite quick, add no dependencies, remove any temporary files your tests create, and keep `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passing.

checks.cmd: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && test "$(cat tests/*.py | grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*def[[:space:]]+test_')" -ge 13

rubric.criterion: The added tests pin observable values, returned state, and failure status instead of only exercising lines (code cannot check this because assertion intent is semantic).
